    <title>Fine-grained Attention and Feature-sharing Generative Adversarial Networks for Single Image Super-Resolution</title>
    <updated>2020-12-24T14:21:22Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10773v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/1911.10773v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>The traditional super-resolution methods that aim to minimize the mean square error usually produce the images with over-smoothed and blurry edges, due to the lose of high-frequency details. In this paper, we propose two novel techniques in the generative adversarial networks to produce photo-realistic images for image super-resolution. Firstly, instead of producing a single score to discriminate images between real and fake, we propose a variant, called Fine-grained Attention Generative Adversarial Network for image super-resolution (FASRGAN), to discriminate each pixel between real and fake.
